channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Ebola en RDC, une épidémie hors de contrôle ?
item.description: Dans cet épisode d’Afrique 360°, Enrica Picco et Rinaldo Depagne reçoivent Frédéric Manantsoa Lai, coordinateur des urgences pour Médecins Sans Frontières, et Onesphore Sematumba, analyste senior pour la République démocratique du Congo et le Burundi à Crisis Group, pour parler de l’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC et de ses conséquences sur la population congolaise, déjà marquée par des années de conflit.

item.title: Avrupa Birliği ve Türkiye: Savunmada Birlik?
item.description: İkinci Dünya Savaşı sonrasında şekillenen uluslararası düzen giderek çözülürken, Ankara ve diğer Avrupa başkentlerindeki yetkililer güvenlik alanında birlikte hareket etmedikleri takdirde ciddi risklerle karşı karşıya kalacaklarının giderek daha fazla farkına varıyor. Tehdit algıları farklılık gösterse de, pragmatik ve esnek iş birliği yolları geliştirmeleri hâlâ mümkün. Avrupa Birliği ve Türkiye: Savunmada Birlik?

item.title: Spain's Ceuta seeks transfer of unaccompanied migrant minors to mainland Spain after border rush
item.description: Though the vast majority of migrants have since returned to Morocco, roughly 1,100 unaccompanied minors who arrived before and during the influx. and cannot be summarily deported. remain, according to the local government Spain's Ceuta seeks transfer of unaccompanied migrant minors to mainland Spain after border rush.

item.title: 'Failure Is Not An Option' In Russia-Ukraine War
item.description: In an interview with RFE/RL, US Senator John Curtis, a Republican from Utah, said there is strong bipartisan support for new legislation sanctioning Russia, stressing that a Russian victory in Ukraine would have negative repercussions elsewhere in the world. 'Failure Is Not An Option' In Russia-Ukraine War.

item.title: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
item.description: State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and CameroonThe US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean, drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic vacuum at risk of being filled by China. US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum.

item.title: Bangladesh pro-uprising groups turn on each other on second anniversary
item.description: Control of campuses has become a battleground for parties and students groups that led the July 2024 movement which ousted Sheikh Hasina and her government. Rights group says at least 17 people were killed in mob violence in July. Six were killed in political violence, a drop from nine in June Bangladesh pro-uprising groups turn on each other on second anniversary.

item.title: Cambodia human rights, Hormuz invasive species risk, IOM lauds 2025 progress
item.description: Concluding his first official visit to Cambodia, UN independent human rights expert Tom Andrews said he was encouraged by the government’s cooperation but remained concerned about key human rights issues such as the lack of freedom of expression. Cambodia human rights, Hormuz invasive species risk, IOM lauds 2025 progress.

item.title: Tate brothers’ US extradition case a ‘step towards accountability,’ says independent expert
item.description: An independent UN human rights expert has welcomed ongoing proceedings in the United States to extradite “manosphere” bloggers Andrew and Tristan Tate to the United Kingdom, calling the case an important step towards accountability for serious allegations of violence against women and girls. Tate brothers’ US extradition case a ‘step towards accountability,’ says independent expert.

item.title: UN reports deadly month for Ukrainian civilians as Russian attacks intensify
item.description: Russian forces hammered Ukraine with ballistic missiles and long-range drones overnight on Tuesday, killing at least 17 civilians – mainly around Kyiv – and injuring another 44, the UN human rights office in Ukraine reported. UN reports deadly month for Ukrainian civilians as Russian attacks intensify.

item.title: Ambassadors briefed on continuing ISIL terror threat
item.description: The Security Council is meeting on Wednesday to examine the persistent threat posed by the terrorist group ISIL, also known as Dae’sh, to international peace and security. At a conference in June, the acting head of the UN counter-terrorism office stated that Al Qaeda, Da’esh, and their affiliates “remain adaptive and resilient”. Moreover, they are using artificial intelligence and other emerging.

item.title: Russia Launches Deadly Ballistic Missile, Drone Attack On Kyiv Region
item.description: Russia launched a massive overnight attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region with ballistic missiles and drones. At least 17 people were killed, including eight near a train station outside Brovary. The strikes also destroyed major warehouse owned by Ukrainian retailer Epicentr. Russia Launches Deadly Ballistic Missile, Drone Attack On Kyiv Region.

item.title: ​How misinformation and ​a​ hardened immigration policy ​turned Ceuta ​into Europe’s ​latest
item.description: In today’s newsletter: The past week shows how quickly images, rumours and ​right-wing political opportunism can eclipse the facts on the groundGood morning. Last week, an estimated 72,000 migrants began crossing into a tiny Spanish enclave on the tip of Morocco. Within 24 hours, most of them had headed home. At least 88 people died after attempting the crossing, according to local officials.

item.title: Russian Barrage On Kyiv Region Kills 17 Amid Ukraine's Air Defense Missile Shortage
item.description: BROVARY, Ukraine -- Russian overnight drone and ballistic missile strikes killed at least 17 people in the Kyiv region, as Ukraine warned of critical air defense shortages and urged its allies to hasten deliveries of urgently needed air defense missiles. Russian Barrage On Kyiv Region Kills 17 Amid Ukraine's Air Defense Missile Shortage.

item.title: Hundreds in Morocco gather near Ceuta border in anxious wait for missing loved ones
item.description: People hope to see friends or relatives among those still returning as death toll from mass crossing nears 100Hundreds of people have gathered in the northern Moroccan town of Fnideq, near the border with Spain’s Ceuta, flashing photos of their missing loved ones to passersby in the hope of tracking them down. Hundreds in Morocco gather near Ceuta border in anxious wait for missing loved ones.

item.title: New Zealand capital delights in rare snowfall as southern city residents ski down world’s steepest
item.description: Snow falls in Wellington for the first time in 15 years while snow blanketed Dunedin and Christchurch on the country’s south islandTemperatures have plummeted across New Zealand as an Antarctic cold snap hovers over the country, delighting the capital, Wellington, which experienced snow for the first time in 15 years, while giving a southern city’s residents a chance to ski through the streets.

item.title: Putin 'Underestimated Trump's Commitment To Freedom'
item.description: In an interview with RFE/RL, Republican Senator Rick Scott said Russian President Vladimir Putin did not anticipate the strength of US support for Ukraine's war effort, adding that a new sanctions bill is meant to hold Russia accountable. Putin 'Underestimated Trump's Commitment To Freedom'.

item.title: Senator Rick Scott Says Congress Must Hold Russia Accountable
item.description: Influential Republican Senator Rick Scott talks to RFE/RL about why he believes sanctions against Russia should be passed immediately, why Ukraine's military innovations matter for the United States, and why defeating Russia is central to deterring an increasingly coordinated authoritarian bloc. ' Senator Rick Scott Says Congress Must Hold Russia Accountable.

item.title: US in a losing race to replenish depleted missile arsenals
item.description: The US’s multibillion-dollar push to expand interceptor missile production could begin rebuilding depleted stocks, but long manufacturing lead times, industrial bottlenecks and cost imbalances mean the benefits will depend on how quickly new capacity translates into deployable missiles. The US Department of Defense (DoD) signed framework agreements worth over US$3 billion with defense contractors US in a losing race to replenish depleted missile arsenals.

item.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike 'Russia's Amazon' Near St. Petersburg
item.description: Russian authorities claim Ukrainian drones hit multiple Wildberries warehouses in several regions on August 4. Officials reported damage at facilities near St. Petersburg, and in the Tver and Moscow regions. Ukraine's drone commander said at least 15 Wildberries hubs have been hit since mid-July. Ukrainian Drones Strike 'Russia's Amazon' Near St. Petersburg.

item.title: Africans bear the brunt of biodiversity loss
item.description: For millions across Africa and the developing world, the biodiversity crisis is not an abstract problem – it’s the soil that no longer yields bountiful harvests and the fish that no longer return to coastal waters. Africans bear the brunt of biodiversity loss.
